text: What may you keep about a card?

text: When your bank calls you, they say: your card ending seven eight nine zero.
prefix: When your bank calls you, they say: your card ending seven eight nine zero.

text: They never ask for the three digits on the back.

text: Now picture a support engineer who pastes a whole card number into a ticket, to check it with the bank.

text: The number now lives in the ticket's backups, in its search index, and with everyone who reads tickets.

text: Systems should talk about cards the way your bank does.

text: The long number on the front of the card is the P A N, the card's own number.

text: The code on the back is never kept by anyone once a payment is approved.

text: Screens and logs may show the masked number: the first six digits and the last four, with nothing between.

text: Other systems keep a card token.

text: A card token is a random name the card vault gives the card.

text: A token is a short prefix plus sixteen random bytes, written in hex.
